piece_type: DTC TV ad (“A Game 60 TV Ad Pool Out 2025”)
regs_in_letter: FD&C Act (no CFR section cited in letter text)

cases.claim: “Playdate? You bring your A-game;” | “Ready to score? You bring your A-game;” | “Bring your A-game to your sexual wellness.” | “You bring your A-game to everything you do. Ask your doctor about APRETUDE.”
cases.context: Scenes of sexually suggestive behavior throughout; PI W&P says Apretude is used as part of a comprehensive prevention strategy including safer sex practices and condoms. Ad includes “APRETUDE does not prevent other sexually transmitted infections. Practice safer sex to reduce your risk.”
cases.rationale: Misleadingly suggests Apretude provides a sense of sexual freedom without the need to practice safer sex to reduce STI risk; the disclaimer does not mitigate the overall impression.
cases.check: Pairwise judge: does the net impression of copy+visuals undercut a labeled safety behavior (e.g., safer sex/condom use) even if a disclaimer is present?

cases.claim: frequent scene changes and attention-grabbing visuals (e.g., the sexually suggestive behaviors described above) during the presentation of the major statement
cases.rationale: Interferes with comprehension of the major statement.
cases.check: Storyboard check: count scene cuts during major statement; judge whether visuals compete with risk audio.
